text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif vowed to make Pakistan prosperous and strong.
- Wheat is being smuggled to Afghanistan from Baluchistan province.
- Nawaz Sharif is expected to visit United States in September.
- Pakistani government has alerted security agencies to be vigiliant against terrorism directed towards embassies.
- Banks have raised their service charges for pay orders, refund of lost travellers cheques, international banking, remittances, imports and bank charges for government business.
- Ousted prime minister Benazir Bhutto met South African President Nelson Mandela in London.
- Commerce Minister Ishaq Dar has termed the decision of the European Union to impose anti-dumping duties on Pakistani grey closth as highly discriminatory and unjustified.
- Pakistan is expected to finalise $2.0 billion worth gas pipeline deal with Iran to fulfil its gas requirements into the next century, Finance Minister Sartaj Aziz said.
- The trade deficit, in financial year ending June 30, 1997 expanded sharply by a record nine percent as it jumped to $3.37 billion from $3.09 billion in 1995/96.
- Soyabean oil prices dipped in the local edible oil market amid a sharp rise in its import, dealers said.
- Trade policy for the year 1997/98 (July-June) will be announced on Wednesday, sources said.
- Pakistan will need to import five million tonnes of wheat annually by the year 2005, a report by Food and Agriculture Organisation said.
